column1: # ONE file, read by hex_grid's loft tests AND by moros's test/lattice.test.js,
# so the two live implementations of the convention cannot drift in silence.
# Regenerating it to make a test pass is the one thing that defeats it.
# (col,row) is pointy-top ODD-R OFFSET. (k,m) is the exact doubled integer
# lattice point:  k = 2*col + (row & 1),  m = 3*row,  centre = (k*sqrt(3)/2, m/2).
# INTEGERS ON PURPOSE: a half-hex parity drift is a drift of 1 in k, visible with
# no epsilon at all. Two implementations computing the same float by different
# expression trees can differ in the last ulp and still be right, so a float
# fixture would have to carry a tolerance -- and a tolerance is where a real
# NEGATIVE ROWS ARE THE POINT. `row % 2 == 1` is false for -1 in both JavaScript
# and Python, so the odd-row shift silently stops below zero; `row & 1` is 1.
# That bug was live in html/hex-lattice.js when this fixture was written.
